Description

Manos Overview

Manos Software Group is part of Valsoft Corporation, a long-term investor in vertical market software businesses. Valsoft acquires and operates software companies with a permanent ownership mindset, emphasizing autonomy, disciplined growth, and long-term value creation. Manos focuses on healthcare-adjacent verticals, including dental, medical, and veterinary software, as well as solutions serving the service industry and GovTech sectors.

Position Description

As we continue to expand our portfolio of vertical market software businesses, we are seeking a dynamic and experienced professional to join our team as Managing Director. Reporting directly to one of our Investment Partners, the Managing Director will be responsible for managing and growing their businesses, with full ownership and accountability for the business. The ideal candidate will be a strategic leader capable of driving operational excellence, organic growth and profitability, while fostering collaboration across teams to ensure the successful execution of business strategies.

Key Responsibilities

Business strategy and operations

Execute within our operating model based on four pillars: strategy and positioning
of the business, operational excellence, growth, and product strategy and technology.
Identify, define and execute strategies required to achieve growth plans and operating objectives, with a focus on continuous improvement.
Drive operational efficiency and excellence and enhance scalability across your portfolio of businesses to optimize performance and maximize profitability.
Drive revenue growth by identifying and supporting new opportunities and growth strategies, including cross-selling and penetrating new markets.
Drive initiatives and solve challenges related to sales, customer success and research and development within your portfolio of businesses.
Prioritize customer satisfaction and retention by ensuring strong solutions, service delivery and customer support within your portfolio companies.
Ensure your portfolio companies have clear product roadmaps established and executed on, balancing investments in research and development with maintenance to maximize new customer growth while retaining existing customers.
Oversee the development and execution of comprehensive product strategies aligned with market trends and the business objectives of the companies in your portfolio.

Financial management

Assume P&L responsibility and focus on achieving key financial metrics related to revenue, ROI, EBITDA, customer retention, etc.
Manage capital allocation and ensure efficient financial management of your portfolio companies, including on a monthly, quarterly and annual basis.

Building effective teams

Build, coach and lead high-performing teams within your portfolio companies.
Cultivate a culture of performance, continuous improvement, collaboration and innovation.
Provide clear direction and motivate teams toward achieving key milestones and
delivering measurable results.

Candidate Profile

Experience

6+ years’ experience in management consulting and/or experience in a technology or software business.
Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, engineering, economics, or any other relevant field.
Master of Business Administration (MBA) (a strong asset).
Relevant experience as a business operations leader with a commercial, customer centric and continuous improvement mindset.
Experience in one or more of the following areas: sales (customer acquisition, market penetration), customer service (support and professional services), product development (research and development) (an asset).
Financial acumen (P&L management, budget, forecast).
People-centric leader with experience successfully building, leading, developing, and mentoring a high performing team.
Experience mobilizing people toward a common goal.
Strong strategic thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to translate vision into
actionable plans and drive results.

Personal Characteristics

Entrepreneurial spirit, results oriented, driven, proactive and a team player.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and adapt to change with agility.
High degree of accountability and ownership of your work.
Strategic and hands-on.

Ready to join a collaborative and innovative team where you can make an immediate impact?

jobs.description:
Job Description

Ready to build your career? We want to hear from you.

Under the leadership of the Vice President, Integrated Management Systems, the Director, Enterprise Solutions – Finance and Operations is responsible for the strategy, evolution, operations, and value creation of the platforms that support Pomerleau’s finance functions and construction operations.

This mandate includes platforms that support accounting, payroll, accounts payable and receivable, procurement, project financial management, and construction operations. It encompasses both the operation and enhancement of current platforms, including CMiC and Procore, as well as the transformation associated with the deployment of the new financial system and the future PMIS.

The Director defines the portfolio roadmap, ensures business continuity throughout the transformation, and prepares the processes, data, integrations, teams, and operating model required to support future platforms.

Working closely with the Finance function and Construction business units, the Director translates business priorities into functional and technology capabilities, ensuring that platforms effectively meet organizational needs.

The Director leads the functional and technical teams, as well as external partners, responsible for platform evolution, integration, operations, and support. They are accountable for platform stability, performance, user adoption, and the value generated for the organization.

What you will do

Finance And Construction Operations

Act as the owner of the portfolio of platforms supporting Finance functions and Construction Operations.
Be accountable for the satisfaction of Finance functions and Construction business units with respect to the capabilities provided.
Understand challenges related to accounting, payroll, accounts payable and receivable, procurement, project financial management, and construction execution in order to guide priorities.
Ensure that business functions and operating sectors have the platforms, data, and processes required to achieve their objectives.
Continuously measure and improve the value generated by the platforms.

Portfolio Strategy And Evolution

Define the long-term vision for Finance and Operations platforms.
Develop a multi-year roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and the priorities of Finance functions and Construction business units.
Anticipate the evolution of financial practices, including payroll, accounts payable and receivable, accounting, procurement, project management, and construction operations.
Define the investments and priorities required to evolve the portfolio.
Maintain the right balance between business continuity, immediate needs, and future capabilities.

Finance And PMIS Transformation

Play a leading role in the design and deployment of the new financial system and future PMIS.
Ensure the continuity, stability, and evolution of CMiC and Procore throughout the transformation.
Plan the transition, data migration, integrations, and coexistence of current and future platforms.
Partner with Finance functions and Construction business units to transform processes and realize expected business benefits.
Prepare teams, operating models, and internal capabilities required to support the new platforms.
Manage risks, dependencies, and operational impacts associated with the transformation.

Practice Leadership

Lead the functional, technical, integration, and development teams responsible for the platforms.
Develop the internal capabilities required to operate and evolve the portfolio.
Oversee capacity planning and resource management for internal teams and external partners.
Foster a culture focused on service excellence, business partnership, accountability, and value creation.

Software Governance And Architecture

Establish functional and technical governance for the platforms within the portfolio.
Ensure alignment with enterprise architecture standards and technology frameworks.
Provide direction on platform configurations, custom development, integrations, and extensions.
Collaborate with architecture, data, integration, and cybersecurity teams to ensure robust, secure, and scalable platforms.
Ensure consistency of processes, data, and integrations across the portfolio.

Delivery And Operational Performance

Be accountable for the availability, stability, security, and performance of the platforms.
Ensure initiatives are delivered on time, within budget, and achieve expected outcomes.
Implement governance and performance monitoring mechanisms at the operational, tactical, and strategic levels.
Manage risks, issues, and dependencies across the portfolio.
Ensure the quality, adoption, and business value realization of deployed platforms.

Vendor And Partner Management

Define the strategy for leveraging software vendors, systems integrators, consultants, and specialized partners.
Manage relationships with strategic vendors and partners.
Participate in contract negotiations and agreement management.
Optimize value delivered by external partners and the cost of platforms and services.
Establish a sustainable balance between internal capabilities and external expertise.

This role could be for you if you have

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field.
Minimum of 10 years of experience managing complex enterprise platforms.
Significant experience with an ERP, financial system, or PMIS.
Experience with solutions supporting multiple financial functions, including accounting, payroll, accounts payable, accounts receivable, procurement, and project financial management.
Strong understanding of financial and operational processes and their translation into integrated technology capabilities.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and external partners.
Experience managing large-scale transformation programs.

Strategic leadership
Customer focus and value creation
Understanding of financial functions and processes, including payroll, accounts payable, and accounts receivable

Our success is built on the passion, expertise, and dedication of our people. Together, we embrace strong execution, innovation, and continuous improvement — values that come to life through the unique talents and collaborative spirit of every team member. If you’re inspired to make a difference through future-building projects, join our best-in-class team.

What is the Opportunity?

Aecon is seeking a Project Controls Director to join the Urban Transportations Solutions group to support dynamic, transit projects in Canada. We are proud to support projects that are committed to faster and more convenient travel, ultimately improving transportation experiences. This starts with bringing aboard the best possible team!

Reporting to the Project Director, the Project Controls Director will provide a single, integrated view of project performance - cost, schedule, risk, data structure, and reporting - to keep the project on track and enable timely decision-making

Lead the project controls function for collaborative delivery models such as Alliance, Progressive Design-Build, CMGC, and other open-book or target-price environments, ensuring alignment with project objectives, commercial frameworks, and governance requirements.
Develop, implement, and maintain the Project Controls Management Plan, defining the project’s approach to cost management, schedule management, estimating, change control, risk management, earned value, reporting, and forecasting.

Lead development and maintenance of project budgets, cost baselines, commitment tracking, accruals, forecasts, contingency usage, and estimate at completion, ensuring timely visibility into financial performance and emerging trends.
Lead development and maintenance of integrated project schedules across design, procurement, construction, systems installation, testing, commissioning, and closeout, including critical path analysis, resource planning, schedule quality reviews, and recovery planning.
Establish progress measurement strategies, including rules of credit, productivity tracking, earned value methodologies, and variance verification processes to ensure performance is measured consistently and accurately.
Implement and maintain Earned Value Management practices to monitor cost and schedule performance, analyze CPI, SPI, SV, and EAC movements, and provide meaningful insight into the drivers behind project results.
Support Target Value Delivery and target proposal development through continuous estimating, trend management, cost modeling, risk integration, and alignment of target cost, schedule, contingency, and commercial assumptions.
Lead the estimating process through development and delivery, ensuring estimates are progressively refined as scope matures, quantities are verified, pricing is tested, and risk is incorporated into the overall forecast and target price.
Own the project’s quantitative risk program, including QCRA, QSRA, Monte Carlo analysis, risk registers, confidence modeling, and integration of risk outputs into cost, schedule, and contingency strategies.
Establish and lead risk governance cadences, facilitate risk reviews, support risk owners in defining mitigation actions, and ensure risks are escalated appropriately with transparent reporting of exposure and confidence levels.
Lead development and implementation of the project-specific change management plan, ensuring scope changes, trend items, baseline changes, contingency draws, and budget transfers are identified, evaluated, approved, and reported in accordance with contract requirements and internal standards.
Deliver integrated reporting and analytics that clearly connect cost, schedule, risk, progress, and change, including executive-level performance narratives, monthly status reporting, dashboarding, milestone reviews, and leadership presentations.
Produce clear, fact-based reporting for project leadership, joint venture stakeholders, and client representatives, highlighting performance drivers, forecast movements, risks, and required decisions or corrective actions.
Lead project controls meetings and reporting cadences to communicate project status, challenge assumptions, align stakeholders, and drive timely corrective actions where performance issues arise.
Partner closely with project leadership, commercial, procurement, design, construction, finance, and client-side controls teams to ensure project controls are integrated into day-to-day project execution rather than functioning as a separate reporting exercise.
Support commercial and procurement teams with subcontractor claims assessments, client claims development, variations, negotiations, and dispute support by ensuring cost, schedule, and risk impacts are properly quantified and documented.
Build strong working relationships with contracting authority counterparts, owner-side controls teams, joint venture partners, and internal stakeholders to support transparent reporting, shared data confidence, and productive issue resolution.
Lead and develop a high-performing project controls team across planning, scheduling, cost control, estimating, risk, change management, and reporting, providing coaching, performance feedback, and development support.
Foster a team culture grounded in accountability, analytical discipline, continuous improvement, inclusion, and a best-for-project mindset that supports collaborative project outcomes.

What You Bring To The Team

15+ years of progressive project controls experience on major infrastructure programs, with significant experience on large-scale transit, rail, heavy civil, or comparable complex projects.
Minimum 5 years in a senior project controls leadership role such as Project Controls Director, Project Controls Lead, or equivalent on projects exceeding $500M.
Demonstrated experience across the full project lifecycle, including pursuit, development, advancement, target proposal, implementation, testing and commissioning, and closeout.
Proven success leading integrated project controls functions across cost, schedule, estimating, risk, earned value, change management, and reporting on multi-year, multi-disciplinary programs.

Advanced knowledge of Project Controls Management Plans, governance structures, project data setup, reporting cadences, progress claiming strategies, productivity measurement, variance analysis, forecasting, and baseline management.

Description

Managing Director

Remote — Canada or United States | Full-time | Reports to: Managing Partner

About Edelweiss Software Group

Edelweiss Software Group is an operating group of Valsoft Corporation, serving as a permanent basecamp for vertical market software companies. Our philosophy is simple: your company leads; we support the ascent. With a buy-and-hold-forever approach, Edelweiss preserves each company's brand and provides the steady guidance, capital, and resources needed to keep both products and people moving upward. We form long-term strategic alliances with existing management teams — we don't buy to sell — placing a premium on the well-being of customers and employees over short-term goals.

The Role

We are seeking an entrepreneurial and operationally minded Managing Director to lead one of our software businesses. Reporting directly to the Managing Partner, you will own the P&L, set strategic direction, and drive sustained, profitable growth across the product portfolio.

This is a hands-on operator role for a leader who can build as much as run. The business is at an exciting inflection point, with a stable core and a new generation of products moving toward market. You will define and execute the strategy for its next phase — evolving the operating model, sharpening the go-to-market engine, and bringing new products successfully to market — while building a transparent, high-performing, customer-obsessed organization. You will operate with high autonomy, supported by Valsoft's long-term investment model, operational expertise, and global network.

What You'll Lead

Drive the next phase of growth — Expand repeatable, high-quality revenue; refine cross-product go-to-market; and identify new opportunities across markets, segments, and channels.
Steer the product portfolio — Refine clear, market-aligned product roadmaps, bring the next generation of products to market and toward self-sustaining economics, and leverage emerging tools (including AI) to enhance the platform.
Evolve the operating model — Move toward business-unit-level ownership and accountability, with the transparency, discipline, and incentives to scale while improving E2E operational efficiency with the use of AI
Deepen customer value — Improve retention, satisfaction, and lifetime value, and embed a culture of customer-led innovation.
Own performance and outcomes — Take full accountability for revenue, EBITDA, and cash flow, with disciplined capital allocation and predictable financial performance.
Lead and grow the organization — Build and develop a high-performing team and a culture of ownership, accountability, continuous improvement, with a customer-first mindset.

Candidate Profile

Experience

Proven experience as a CEO, Managing Director, COO, VP or General Manager with full P&L ownership of a software or technology business.
P&L scale: Prior P&L accountability of $5M or more.
Team leadership: Experience leading and developing a team of 10 or more.
New-product track record: Has brought new products to market and successfully scaled them.
Track record of scaling and growing established software businesses and of transforming a business.
Strong commercial instinct across sales, pricing, and go-to-market strategy, including cross-sell and market penetration.
Ability to lead across product, operations, and finance, with sound financial acumen (P&L management, budgeting, forecasting).
Comfort with emerging technologies, including AI.
Bachelor's degree in business, finance, engineering, economics, or a related field; an MBA or advanced degree is a strong asset.

Personal characteristics

Empathetic leader:A strong ability to influence others, and an empathetic, active listener.
Entrepreneurial spirit — results-oriented, driven, proactive, and a team player.
Both strategic and hands-on, with the ability to translate vision into actionable plans and drive results.
A high degree of accountability and ownership.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and adapt to change with agility.
A people-centric leader who leads with humility, empathy, and sound judgment.

Why This Opportunity Stands Out

A platform for growth — Lead an established, market-leading business at a genuine inflection point — with the core stabilized and a new product generation ready to scale.
True ownership — Run the business with full autonomy and accountability, empowered to make decisions and drive outcomes.
Long-term backing — Valsoft's buy-and-hold-forever model means you build enduring value rather than managing toward an exit.

Onboard and integrate into Toptal; meet your colleagues and the Solution Architects on your team.
Learn about Toptal’s history, culture, and vision, with a focus on the state of our industry, Toptal’s operating model, and the core messages important to Toptal.

Conduct a comprehensive review of current demand in your practice area, talent that already exists in the network, active engagements, and any work we may already be doing or have done.

Articulate a hypothesis about how to grow the team’s impact (priorities, structure, and standards) and design experiments and execution approaches to get there.

Be in front of clients on a regular basis to hear from them firsthand.
Define the team’s operating model, architecture standards, and pre-sales engagement process.
Build your team and begin positively impacting revenue growth.

Have moved from purely planning to execution.
See an impact from your involvement in early initiatives, including repeatable solutions in market and a growing pipeline supported by your team.
Establish key partner relationships and a clear hiring and talent plan for the team.

In the first year, expect to:

Feel like you made the best decision of your career.
Increase the growth rate of Toptal materially.
Have a high-performing, fully staffed Solution Architect team recognized for Hybrid Cloud and DevOps expertise.

15+ years of experience in cloud, infrastructure, or DevOps engineering and architecture, with at least 5+ years leading teams of solution architects or senior engineers within cloud or technology services.
3+ years managing a business or team, preferably with P&L or budget responsibility, and a proven track record of overseeing financial performance, identifying areas for improvement, and driving profitability and growth.
Proven experience leading and developing teams of solution architects or senior technical consultants.
Proven ability to build and scale hybrid cloud and DevOps service offerings in a consulting, managed services, technology services, or enterprise environment.
Deep expertise in hybrid and multi-cloud architecture across AWS, Azure, and/or Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including connectivity, identity, governance, and workload placement across on-premises, private cloud, and public cloud environments.
Strong experience with data center and virtualization platforms (e.g., VMware, Nutanix, Hyper-V) and hybrid cloud technologies (e.g., Azure Arc, AWS Outposts, Google Distributed Cloud).
Deep knowledge of cloud-native technologies, including containerization and orchestration (Kubernetes, OpenShift, Docker), serverless computing, and microservices architecture.
Strong experience with Infrastructure-as-Code and configuration management tools such as Terraform, Ansible, CloudFormation, or Pulumi.

Expertise in DevOps and platform engineering practices, including DevSecOps, site reliability engineering (SRE), observability, and the use of delivery metrics (e.g., DORA) to drive improvement.

Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Role Overview

As our VP of Sales - Global Public Sector, you will spearhead year-over-year global revenue growth by developing and executing on enterprise level PUBSEC customer acquisition strategies. You will drive long-term success through strategic development, coaching, and expanding Cohere’s presence in the public sector. In this pivotal leadership role, you will cultivate and guide our sales team to exceed revenue targets and organizational goals, while fostering a culture of excellence and innovation.

Key Responsibilities

As our VP of Public Sector Sales you will:

Develop, execute, and lead a comprehensive, global go-to-market growth strategy and sales plan for the Public Sector, driving revenue growth and market expansion working with other regional sales teams.
Provide sales and operational leadership to Cohere’s PUBSEC sales team, ensuring alignment with company objectives and priorities.
Partner with Marketing, Product, and Engineering teams to synchronize sales efforts with broader company goals.
Represent Cohere at PUBSEC industry events, conferences, and networking opportunities, as well as with regulators and government agencies, in collaboration with other regional and global leaders in Cohere.
Manage and nurture relationships with government decision-makers and partners to ensure Cohere’s success in the region. Identify and pursue new business opportunities, negotiating and closing high-value deals.
Collaborate with global teams to strengthen anchor relationships and establish best practices for enterprise-level project implementations, ensuring strong client engagement throughout project lifecycles.

Qualifications

This career opportunity may be a good match for you if you:

Have 10+ years of PUBSEC sales and leadership experience leading go-to-market efforts and driving revenue growth for fast paced technology organizations.
Have an established network, including federal agencies, prime contractors, and industry associations with an emphasis on the Defense and Intelligence communities.
Possess a proven track record of leading capture and sales efforts for consultative solution sales and business development efforts, with a deep understanding of regional procurement and budget cycles, customer success, and resource allocation.
Have exceptional communication and leadership skills, with the ability to build cross-functional relationships and influence at all levels.
Are comfortable operating in a matrix environment, coordinating efforts across cross-functional teams and regions without the need for a large direct organization.
Are a self-starter with an entrepreneurial mindset, capable of working independently, rolling up sleeves, and driving impact as a ‘builder.’
Experience in AI or a related industry is highly desirable.
Must be willing to travel (25-40%).

Working Location:

This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.
Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.
For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.
For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.
Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. National Director, Technical Services

Mississauga, ON

The Opportunity

Reporting to the National Vice President, Technical Services & Sustainability, the National Director, Technical Services is a key leader within BGO’s Operational Excellence function, responsible for establishing, executing, influencing, driving adoption and advancing the national technical standards, programs, priorities, and performance measures that enable consistent, safe, efficient, compliant, and high-performing building operations across BGO’s Canadian portfolio (Commercial, Retail, Residential, Industrial).

The National Director provides national leadership and oversight of the Regional Technical Services team, maintaining a portfolio-wide view of building operations, compliance, technical risk, asset performance, training, emergency preparedness, building systems, and Operations CAPEX and lifecycle requirements.

The Director translates portfolio needs, business priorities, operational intelligence and performance data into national programs, standards and measurable outcomes. The role establishes clear expectations for Regional Technical Services Managers, provides strategic technical guidance to Property Management and Building Operations, and identifies opportunities for standardization, performance improvement, innovation and value creation.

Technical Services is a core pillar of Operational Excellence, providing the technical governance, standards, expertise and performance oversight required to enable safe, consistent, efficient and high-performing building operations across the portfolio.

This is an onsite position located in Mississauga, ON.

What You Will Do

Set the national Technical Services strategy and align regional priorities with BGO’s business and operational objectives.
Lead and develop regional Technical Services teams, establishing clear accountability, performance expectations, and capability development.
Own national standards, programs, and KPIs to ensure consistent, compliant, and high-performing building operations across the portfolio.
Oversee technical risk, compliance, and life safety, including inspections, maintenance, emergency preparedness, and the FOREVERREADY program.
Drive continuous improvement and operational excellence using audits, data, KPIs, incidents, and stakeholder feedback.
Build technical capabilities and training across building operations, technology, compliance, maintenance, energy, and decarbonization.
Provide portfolio-level asset and CAPEX advice, identifying major system risks, lifecycle needs, investment priorities, and required interventions.
Advance digital transformation and innovation, leveraging operational data, analytics, AI, and smart-building technologies to improve performance and value.
Advise senior leadership through evidence-based recommendations focused on risk reduction, operational improvement, investment, and ROI.

Other related duties at this location or other BGO locations as required.

Who You Are

Key Qualifications

Education: Degree in Engineering, Building Science, Facilities Management, or a related discipline (or equivalent experience).
Experience: 10+ years of progressive experience in technical services, engineering, or building operations within commercial real estate, including experience leading technical teams and multi-site programs.
Licences / Certifications Professional designation (P.Eng, PMP, CFM, or similar) considered an asset
Industry / Functional Knowledge:
Strong knowledge of multi-residential, office, retail, and industrial building systems.
Demonstrated experience in technical program development, performance management, capital and lifecycle planning, regulatory compliance, and risk management across a multi-site portfolio.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Yardi, AI and Property Technology and building systems.

Other Skills And Behaviours

Portfolio Leadership: Connect regional performance, asset needs, risks, and data to set national priorities and identify systemic issues.
Technical & Decision Excellence: Apply sound technical judgment while balancing safety, compliance, reliability, lifecycle, operational impact, and cost.
Program & Performance Leadership: Establish national standards, programs, KPIs, and performance expectations, driving consistency and continuous improvement.
People & Capability Leadership: Lead Regional Technical Services Managers, build team capability, and establish consistent training and operating practices.
Strategic Advisory & Risk Leadership: Clearly communicate technical risks, capital needs, and priorities while maintaining national oversight of significant risks and emergency readiness
Valid Driver's License and access to a reliable vehicle.
Police Clearance: A criminal verification check is required for employment

Who We Are

BGO is a global leader in real estate investment management, partnering with more than 750 institutional clients to invest in and manage high-quality real estate across office, industrial, residential, retail, and hospitality sectors. With a presence in 28 cities across 12 countries, BGO combines deep local expertise with global reach to unlock value in real estate markets worldwide. As part of SLC Management and Sun Life, BGO brings the strength, scale, and trusted expertise of one of the world's leading financial services organizations.

For more information, please visit www.bgo.com

Why join us

At BGO, you'll be part of a collaborative team that values your growth, supports your success, and empowers you to make a meaningful impact. We offer a competitive total rewards package, including comprehensive benefits and an annual discretionary bonus. You'll work in a supportive, team-oriented environment with access to ongoing learning, mentorship, and professional development opportunities to help you grow your career.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

As a leading Canadian wealth management organization, Richardson Wealth offers the personal touch of a boutique firm while delivering big results. With offices across the country, we are home to some of Canada’s best investment advisors. We’ve embarked on an exciting growth phase – a multi-year transformational journey to enhance our entrepreneurial, high-performing, advisor-centric culture.

Position Overview

Reporting to the VP National Sales Manager and Head of Advisor Experience, this role serves as a trusted right-hand partner, helping translate strategic priorities into coordinated programs and execution across the advisor network. The AVP will build and enhance advisor programs, shape the branch leadership communications strategy, and work closely with cross-functional partners to deliver firm-wide initiatives that strengthen advisor engagement, productivity, growth, and client experience.

This is an existing vacancy

Duties And Responsibilities

Serve as the trusted right-hand partner to the National Sales Manager and Head of Advisor Experience, translating strategic priorities into practical plans, programs, and coordinated execution
Lead the strategy, design, launch, and continuous improvement of advisor programs spanning onboarding, development, practice management, growth, recognition, and engagement
Develop and manage a branch leadership communications strategy, including message architecture, leadership forums, editorial planning, communication channels, and governance
Partner with Distribution Leadership, Compliance, Operations, Technology, Marketing, and other functions to coordinate the execution of firm-wide initiatives across the advisor and branch network
Lead change management for advisor-facing initiatives, including stakeholder alignment, readiness planning, communications, training, field engagement, launch support, and sustained adoption
Support the strategic direction and evolution of the branch operating model, including Tier 1 compliance responsibilities, role clarity, decision rights, and effective collaboration across branch and corporate functions
Create clear operating rhythms, decision forums, roadmaps, and accountability mechanisms to keep interdependent initiatives aligned and moving forward
Establish measures of program adoption, advisor proficiency, engagement, and business outcomes, using feedback and insights to continuously improve delivery
Lead cross-functional planning for national meetings, branch leadership forums, and strategic events that reinforce priorities and strengthen culture
Champion improvements to the advisor and client experience by simplifying communications and processes and scaling effective practices across branches
Provide leadership, coaching, and direction to team members and project partners, building the capabilities required to execute at scale

Qualifications

Progressive leadership experience in roles working directly with advisors, branch leaders, and senior distribution executives, with a demonstrated ability to build trust and influence outcomes
Extensive wealth management experience and a strong understanding of advisor practices, branch operations, investment products, client service, growth strategies, and the Canadian regulatory environment
Proven success leading complex change in an advisor-led business model, from strategy and stakeholder alignment through implementation, adoption, and reinforcement
Demonstrated experience designing and scaling advisor programs, communications, enablement, or practice-management initiatives with measurable business impact
Strong strategic planning, program leadership, and execution skills, with the ability to manage multiple interdependent priorities in a complex, matrixed organization
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop clear, practical messaging for branch leaders and advisors
A collaborative, hands-on leadership style, sound judgment, and the confidence to act as a trusted partner to senior leadership
An asset for the individual to meet all applicable CIRO proficiency, experience, and registration requirements to be approved and maintain registration as a supervisor

The expected annualized base salary range for this role is $190,000-$225,000. The actual salary offered will take into consideration a wide array of factors including, but not limited to, the individual’s skill, experience, education and training, and the consideration of internal equity. Richardson offers a competitive total rewards package in addition to the base pay (where applicable), which includes a performance-based incentive plan, comprehensive health & dental benefits, a group RRSP matching plan and paid time off.

Our firm is only as good as the people who work here. Our employees are exceptional because they combine in-depth expertise with enthusiasm, and empathy. From our front office talent to our colleagues behind the scenes, we have one focus: to ensure our people thrive here more than anywhere else. Are you innovative, self-driven, and client-centric?
